text.arabic_uthmani: ءَأَنتُمْ أَنزَلْتُمُوهُ مِنَ ٱلْمُزْنِ أَمْ نَحْنُ ٱلْمُنزِلُونَ

words.gloss_range: interrogative hamza fused to an independent second-person plural pronoun; the word foregrounds the addressees as the disputed agent

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the following verb whose subject is the challenged addressees
the answering alternative that completes the binary question

words.prose: {{ar:ءَأَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:a-antum}}) begins by joining the question force to the human addressee in one surface word, so the ayah opens on disputed agency rather than on the occurrence of rain. The independent pronoun stands in the nominative subject slot before {{ar:أَنزَلْتُمُوهُ}} ({{tr:anzaltumūhu}}), making the addressees syntactically visible as the proposed cause even though the rhetoric will deny that claim. Its opening hamza scopes forward to the later {{ar:أَمْ نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:am naḥnu}}), so the question is a single binary challenge: humans are momentarily placed in the agent slot in order for the divine counter-claim to remove them from it. The sound break at the beginning also turns the prior observation of water (56:68) into an immediate confrontation over who sent it down.

topics.headline: fronted addressee becomes the disputed agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah is not asking whether water descended, but whether the addressed humans can occupy the agent role.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as an interrogative particle plus nominative second-person plural pronoun, and attachment evidence makes the following verb phrase its predicate clause.

topics.headline: hamza opens a denial-bearing binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first word opens a question whose answer is already structured by the later human-versus-divine alternative.
topics.reason: The opening hamza is paired with the disjunctive particle in word 5, and the attachment constraints identify the second clause as the coordinated alternative.

topics.headline: question particle and pronoun arrive together
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the challenge before the verb appears because question force and human addressee are fused at the opening.
topics.reason: The surface combines the interrogative hamza with the independent pronoun, making the opening word carry both challenge and addressee focus.

topics.headline: prior water observation becomes an agency question
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that 56:69 completes the prior water reflection by turning it into a question about source and agency.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence links the ayah's contrast refrain to the preceding water question and confirms that the opening challenge is not detached from 56:68.

words.gloss_range: Form IV perfect causative descent with second-person plural subject and a third-person object suffix referring back to the water of 56:68
words.root_gloss_range: descent, causing descent, sending down, arrival, lodging, and prepared provision; the local verb selects causative rain-descent from clouds while preserving controlled-transfer pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the source complement of the descent verb
the final participial title answering the same root and form field

words.prose: {{ar:أَنزَلْتُمُوهُ}} ({{tr:anzaltumūhu}}) compresses the challenged human subject, the completed causative act, and the prior water-object into one verb. Its perfect form treats the descent as an acknowledged occurrence; the dispute is attribution, not whether the water came down. Form IV makes the question sharper than simple falling: it asks whether the addressees caused the water to descend, and the active wording keeps that proposed human agent exposed rather than hidden in a passive. The attached suffix carries the water of 56:68 into the present ayah, while the liaison keeps proposed agents and water-object bound in one pronounceable cluster. The following {{ar:مِنَ ٱلْمُزْنِ}} ({{tr:mina al-muzni}}) narrows the root's broad descent field to physical rain-descent from clouds; revelation and other descent branches stay as field pressure, not the direct local sense. The wider root family still gives the event the feel of controlled transfer along origin, path, and arrival-point, with prepared provision rather than random falling. The same root and causative field return at the close in {{ar:ٱلْمُنزِلُونَ}} ({{tr:al-munzilūna}}), shifting the disputed act from a one-time human claim to a divine agent-title.

topics.headline: completed act is attributed to the challenged addressees
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the descent is treated as a completed fact while the human addressees are pressed as its alleged cause.
topics.reason: QAC identifies a Form IV perfect verb with second-person plural subject marking, and attachment evidence ties that subject to the overt addressee pronoun.

topics.headline: object suffix pulls in the previous water
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the word depends on 56:68 for its object, so the agency challenge remains tied to the water just mentioned.
topics.reason: Cross-reference evidence identifies the masculine singular suffix as resuming the prior water, and translation support warns that it should not be resolved as clouds or addressees.

topics.headline: Form IV asks who initiated descent from clouds
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb is about causing descent from a specified source, not merely observing water falling.
topics.reason: The verb is Form IV, carries an object suffix, and governs the cloud-source complement through word 3.

topics.headline: broad descent field is focused onto rain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that rain is being framed inside the Quranic descent field, while the local object and cloud source prevent revelation or other branches from becoming the direct sense.
topics.reason: V4 shows a wide descent and sending-down family, but the local object suffix and source phrase select rain-descent as the active sense.

topics.headline: descent feels like controlled arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the water is imagined as an arriving provision from above, while the local grammar keeps the meaning anchored in physical precipitation.
topics.reason: The station and provision branches can color the controlled-transfer image, but the verb's object and source keep the local sense from becoming lodging or hospitality.

topics.headline: one word binds proposed agent and water-object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the verb does not hide agency in a passive form; it visibly binds the proposed human subject to the water-object.
topics.reason: The word is active, finite, and suffix-bearing, with the liaison vowel keeping the subject ending and object suffix in one pronounceable cluster.

topics.headline: human verb is answered by divine participle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same root and causative field return at the end, but with the agency moved from alleged human action to divine identity.
topics.reason: Both words share the n-z-l causative field, while QAC distinguishes the first as perfect verb and the final word as active participle.

topics.headline: water observation becomes part of a descent thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the first clause is a complete human-agency challenge inside a wider Surah 56 pattern of descent language (56:56, 56:80, 56:93) and boundary movement.
topics.reason: The clause has subject, verb, object, and source complement, and contextual evidence marks the root as common while local boundary evidence links the water observation to this descent challenge.

words.gloss_range: source-governing preposition; here it marks the cloud phrase as the origin or channel of the descent

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the verb to which the source phrase attaches

words.prose: {{ar:مِنَ}} ({{tr:mina}}) is the small hinge that turns the first clause from generic water-production into descent from a specified source. It governs {{ar:ٱلْمُزْنِ}} ({{tr:al-muzni}}) and attaches the whole phrase to {{ar:أَنزَلْتُمُوهُ}} ({{tr:anzaltumūhu}}), so the clouds are not a loose scene-setting detail but the origin frame of the challenged action. The source sense is primary here; any medium or channel nuance remains inside that origin relation because the grammar marks a governed cloud complement. Its invariant prepositional form and the repeated m/n sounds bind the particle to the cloud noun as one compact source phrase. By coming after the object-bearing verb, the particle moves the listener from the already mentioned water toward the high, inaccessible starting point of its descent.

topics.headline: preposition fixes the clouds as source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud phrase is governed as the origin of descent, not a free description of the scene.
topics.reason: QAC and attachment evidence identify the particle as governing the genitive cloud noun and attaching that source complement to the verb.

topics.headline: origin sense limits other particle values
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the phrase points to the starting point and channel of descent rather than merely to a portion taken from clouds.
topics.reason: The local grammar and translation support select source or origin; medium nuance can survive only as a channel within that source relation.

topics.headline: short particle binds tightly to the cloud noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that one invariant particle creates a compact source phrase with the following cloud word.
topics.reason: The particle has no root, governs the next noun, and forms one postverbal source unit with it.

topics.headline: source phrase completes the human-agency beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first half reaches full shape only after the source phrase, moving from water-object to cloud-origin before the pivot.
topics.reason: The first clause contains the proposed subject, verb, object suffix, and source complement before word 5 introduces the second member.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive rain-cloud source, singular or collective; locally the word specifies water-bearing clouds rather than generic cloud cover
words.root_gloss_range: clouds and cloud-pieces, especially bright or rain-bearing clouds; secondary branches include swift passage and other nonlocal senses, with only cloud-source imagery active here

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the governing preposition that makes the noun a source complement

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُزْنِ}} ({{tr:al-muzni}}) names the cloud-source as a governed genitive complement, so the cloud is not the agent, object, or independent topic of the clause. The definite form points to recognizable rain-bearing clouds, and its singular-or-collective shape can indicate a cloud mass or class rather than one counted cloud. The lexeme is unusually specific: the guardrail evidence supports cloud or bright, water-bearing cloud as the local branch, including a dense, precipitation-capable source image, while broader branches such as swift passage only add transience to the rain-source image and do not replace it. Its one-time Quranic occurrence gives this exact cloud term extra concentration at the point where source specificity drives the challenge. Because this rare cloud word follows the object-bearing descent verb, it disambiguates the water of 56:68 as rain-water and pulls the scene upward from drinkable water to the source humans can see but cannot command.

topics.headline: cloud noun is source complement, not agent
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the clouds are grammatically the source channel of descent, while agency remains with the contrasted subjects.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as genitive after the preposition, and attachment evidence identifies it as the source complement of the descent verb.

topics.headline: lexeme selects water-bearing cloud
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah chooses a specialized rain-cloud term rather than a generic cloud word.
topics.reason: V4's accepted local branch gives clouds and bright clouds, and the CRITICAL rows distinguish this lexeme from broader cloud vocabulary.

topics.headline: cloud image carries density and passing movement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a rain-source that is heavy with water yet transient, while the local noun still means cloud rather than motion itself.
topics.reason: The accepted cloud branch licenses the water-bearing image; secondary swift-passage evidence can color the source as mobile but cannot govern the local sense.

topics.headline: definite collective form broadens source scale
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the source can be heard as the familiar rain-cloud mass or class, not merely one counted cloud.
topics.reason: QAC marks the noun as definite and singular or collective, and the supplied lexical rows contrast the collective form with a unit cloud.

topics.headline: rare cloud word concentrates the source argument
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that a one-time Quranic cloud lexeme is placed precisely where source specificity drives the agency challenge.
topics.reason: The contextual profile marks the root and noun form as a single occurrence, and the row evidence ties that rarity to the water challenge.

topics.headline: cloud source specifies the previous water
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the cloud-source phrase makes the water of 56:68 specifically rain-water.
topics.reason: The prior object is water, and the governed cloud noun supplies the source that narrows that referent across the ayah boundary.

topics.headline: first beat ends at the high source
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first clause lifting attention from drinkable water to elevated cloud-source before the divine-agent pivot.
topics.reason: Word order places the cloud source at the end of the first beat, and the compact sound-shape supports the dense source image without creating an independent topic.

words.gloss_range: disjunctive conjunction; here it is the hinge of the human-versus-divine agency question, with connected-disjunction force and possible corrective coloring

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the opening hamza-pronoun that licenses the disjunctive pair
the divine pronoun that begins the second member

words.prose: {{ar:أَمْ}} ({{tr:am}}) is the central hinge of the ayah. Paired with the opening hamza, it makes the question a two-member contrast: did the addressees cause the descent, or is the divine speaker the sender-down? The connected-disjunction reading gives the structure a closed binary, while the licensed corrective reading lets the second half sound like a redirection from the human proposal to the divine answer. As an independent particle between two complete agency frames, it keeps the clauses distinct and marks the exact pivot from everything attributed to the addressees to everything claimed by the divine speaker. Its brevity also creates a short audible reset before the compact divine self-identification.

topics.headline: paired particle creates a closed binary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah structurally permits a choice between human and divine agency, not a blended third agency.
topics.reason: QAC identifies the particle as disjunctive and the attachment constraints make the second member a coordinated alternative to the first.

topics.headline: alternative can sound corrective
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second clause can be heard as more than option two: it corrects the attempted human-agency claim.
topics.reason: The bundle licenses a disconnected or corrective reading, but QAC's local grammar supplies connected disjunction as the main parse.

topics.headline: disjunction excludes middle agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the question itself produces the denial by routing uncertainty into the divine side of the contrast.
topics.reason: The paired question and disjunctive particle confine the agency claim to mutually exclusive alternatives.

topics.headline: standalone particle pivots the two beats
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the exact surface point where the ayah turns from the human clause to the divine clause.
topics.reason: The particle appears as its own word between the complete first clause and the divine pronoun that opens the second.

topics.headline: brief hinge resets the sound before the divine pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a short audible reset before the compact divine counter-claim.
topics.reason: The particle is a short independent conjunction that links but separates the two agency clauses.

words.gloss_range: independent first-person plural divine pronoun; it opens the second nominal clause as the true agent identity

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the disjunctive particle after which the divine counter-clause begins
the matched human pronoun across the binary question
the participial predicate agreeing with the divine pronoun

words.prose: {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}) starts a fresh second member after {{ar:أَمْ}} ({{tr:am}}), not an apposition inside the human clause. As an independent first-person plural divine pronoun, it gives the speaker a full subject slot before the predicate and balances the earlier human pronoun while reversing the agency verdict. The following {{ar:ٱلْمُنزِلُونَ}} ({{tr:al-munzilūna}}) agrees with it in the nominal predicate frame, so the answer becomes an identity claim: the divine speaker, not the addressees or the clouds, is the sender-down. Its plural form is majesty and self-reference, not a numerical multiplication of agents. It also anchors the boundary movement upward, from human drinking reflection to cloud-source agency and then to divine self-identification.

topics.headline: detached pronoun gives the divine agent its own slot
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine subject is not merely inferred; it stands visibly as the answer-side agent.
topics.reason: QAC identifies an independent first-person plural pronoun and the cross-reference evidence marks it as divine self-reference.

topics.headline: second member begins a nominal identity claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the second half is not another finite event report but a nominal identity predication.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence makes the final participle the predicate of this pronoun and identifies the second clause as the coordinated alternative.

topics.headline: agreement locks the title to the divine pronoun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final title cannot drift back to the clouds or the human addressees because it is grammatically locked to the divine pronoun.
topics.reason: The pronoun functions as subject of the predicate, and the final participle agrees with it in the nominal frame.

topics.headline: plural form carries majesty, not multiple agents
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the plural pronoun is a divine discourse form of authority rather than a count of several senders.
topics.reason: The QAC grammar and cross-reference evidence identify the pronoun as divine self-reference.

topics.headline: matched pronouns make the agency axis
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's balanced surface opposition between the addressed humans and the divine speaker.
topics.reason: Both agency poles are independent pronouns occupying corresponding positions across the disjunctive frame.

topics.headline: scene shifts from human reflection to divine self-claim
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse move from second-person water reflection to first-person divine agency.
topics.reason: The boundary evidence identifies the shift from audience address to divine counter-claim, and this pronoun is the local anchor of that shift.

topics.headline: fronted divine pronoun prepares the final title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine pronoun mirrors the opening human pronoun but receives the stable title that resolves the ayah.
topics.reason: The pronoun precedes its predicate and pairs structurally with the opening human pronoun, while the final title completes only the divine side.

words.gloss_range: definite Form IV active participle predicate, masculine plural nominative; locally an exclusive divine agent-title for causing descent
words.root_gloss_range: descent and sending down, including rain, provision, punishment, revelation, and arrival; the local participle names the agent of causing descent and leaves the object recoverable from the water challenge

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: the divine subject of the predicate
the earlier finite verb answered by this participial title

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْمُنزِلُونَ}} ({{tr:al-munzilūna}}) lands as the ayah's final answer. It is the definite Form IV active participle agreeing with {{ar:نَحْنُ}} ({{tr:naḥnu}}), so the second half identifies the divine speaker as the senders-down rather than reporting a single completed act. The definite predicate and binary frame make the role exclusive: the clouds are the source complement, but the divine speaker holds the agent-title. Because the participle has no overt object suffix, it answers the water case while also naming the broader capacity of causing descent as controlled distribution from source to recipients. The active-participle group is distributionally more marked than the root's many finite verb uses, and parallels at 26:187 and 29:34 keep a sovereign-dispensation coloring without controlling this rain-water setting. It echoes {{ar:أَنزَلْتُمُوهُ}} ({{tr:anzaltumūhu}}) in the same root and causative field, but changes finite alleged human action into enduring divine identity and closes the ayah with the long ū plus final n sound of the agent-title.

topics.headline: definite predicate identifies the true senders-down
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final predicate does not offer a vague description; it claims the identifiable and exclusive sending-down role.
topics.reason: QAC marks the word as definite, nominative active participle predicate, and the binary question excludes the proposed human alternative.

topics.headline: active participle turns descent into identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the answer names a standing agent identity, not merely a past divine action parallel to the human verb.
topics.reason: The local form is a Form IV active participle serving as khabar, preserving causative agency in a noun-like predicate.

topics.headline: agreement keeps the predicate with the divine subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final title is not attached to the cloud-source phrase but to the divine pronoun.
topics.reason: The participle is masculine plural nominative as predicate of the divine pronoun, while the cloud noun is genitive under the preposition.

topics.headline: objectless title exceeds the single water case
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the title answers the rain-water challenge while also naming a broader divine capacity to cause descent.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence licenses the omitted object as recoverable from the first member, while the objectless participle and root field keep the title broader than the single suffix-bound water object.

topics.headline: form choice breaks simple symmetry with the human verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the divine side is not phrased as merely doing once what humans are asked about doing once.
topics.reason: The first descent word is a perfect verb with an object suffix, while the answer uses a definite active participle.

topics.headline: small participle group makes the title marked
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that this active participial title is distributionally more marked than the root's many finite verb uses.
topics.reason: The contextual profile counts the active participle group as small, with divine referent dominance; the inter-ayah examples at 26:187 and 29:34 are valid parallels for sovereign dispensation without controlling this local water sense.

topics.headline: closing title answers the opening descent verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the same root returns at the end with the agency corrected from human claim to divine title.
topics.reason: The final word shares the n-z-l causative field with the earlier verb but changes the grammatical role from finite action to predicate title.

topics.headline: final word lands the ayah on divine agency
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that syntax, echo, restriction, and sound all converge at the final word as the ayah's resolution.
topics.reason: The word is the last element of the ayah and simultaneously functions as predicate, restrictive title, root echo, and closure.

topics.headline: water handoff culminates in divine identity language
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the previous water is carried all the way into a standing divine title.
topics.reason: The water object is recoverable across the clause, and the boundary evidence tracks the move from ordinary drinking to divine self-claim.

topics.headline: predicate belongs to the answer side of the disjunction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final predicate is not merely descriptive but answers the human-agency challenge under the second alternative.
topics.reason: The disjunctive particle introduces the second member, and the participle is the predicate of that member.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Descent from cloud is distinguished from reception below.** Repeated `ن ز ل` activates **B002**, bringing or sending down; `م ز ن` **B001** supplies cloud and cloud-piece. The disjunction assigns the directional action to one of two agents. **Abductive move:** I infer that drinkers can collect water after descent but cannot author the cloud-to-ground movement. **Reading change:** the question isolates atmospheric delivery as a nonhuman causal stage.

2. **Cloud as filled vessel whose contents are released.** `م ز ن` **B004** supplies filling the waterskin, and `ن ز ل` **B001** supplies descent. **Abductive move:** I infer a container analogy connecting cloud, cups (56:18), and bodily drinking. **Reading change:** rain reads as transfer between vessels in a larger provisioning system.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Revelation as `تنزيل` at 56:80 transferred the rain model to speech: both descend from nurturing authority as usable provision.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **Repeated descent language distinguishes receiving water from bringing it down out of cloud.** Finite verb and agent noun repeat `ن ز ل` (B002, causing or sending down), with `م ز ن` (B001, cloud or cloud-piece) as explicit source and *am* dividing human from divine agency. Ayat 64–68 establish the crop’s dependence and the water actually drunk; ayat 70–74 move through drinkability, fire, source-creation, reminder, and praise. The packet supplies source, downward transfer, and rival-agent syntax; I infer that users control neither the initial location nor the transit that makes water available. Access at ground level does not entail authorship of descent.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 56:80 reactivates `ن ز ل` for the noble recitation’s transmission, sharpening descent as governed delivery across both material and verbal provision without collapsing their distinct branches or objects.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesinin ana bölümü bir şeyi düzenleyip kendi yerine koymayı destekler; ancak aynı ifade bölüm bölüm ve tekrar tekrar ulaştırma kullanımını da taşır. identity_judgment.boundary_note: Uygun yere veya sıraya koyma çekirdektir; bölüm bölüm ulaştırma yalnızca açıkça desteklenen özel kullanımda kalır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın düzenleme ve yerine koyma anlamıyla sınırlıdır; başka dallardaki bildiri yapıları bu yalın çekirdeğe ancak ayrı bir kaynak çeşitlemesi olarak bağlanır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi düzenleyerek ona uygun görülen yere, sıraya veya dereceye koymaktır. Aynı biçim, belirli bir bildirim bağlamında içeriği bölüm bölüm ve yineleyerek ulaştırmayı da anlatabilir.

facets.statement: Bir şey düzenlenir ve kendisine uygun yere, sıraya veya dereceye konur.
Belirli bildirim bağlamında içerik parçalara ayrılarak ve tekrar tekrar ulaştırılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynak ifadesi düzenleme ile bir şeyi kendi yerine koymayı ortak çekirdek olarak verir; ayrıca belirli bir bildirim kullanımında içeriğin bölüm bölüm ve tekrarlarla ulaştırılmasını ayrı bir kapsam olarak ekler.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi konuğa hazırlanan yiyecek ve yol azığını çekirdek yapar; konuğun kendisini, ürün gelirini, fazlalığı, bağışı ve birikmiş payı buna bağlı kullanımlar olarak açıkça verir. Verilen dal çerçevesi çekirdeği ve benzetmeli uzantıları doğru ayırmaya elverişlidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Konuk için hazırlanan pay çekirdektir; yer, derece ve savaş anlamları dışarıda, gelir ve bağış anlamları ise bağlı uzantı olarak tutulmalıdır.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın yiyecek, pay, gelir ve konuk adları ile konuk etme ve bolluk bildiren yapılar ayrı ayrı korunur; yapıya bağlı bolluk anlamı bütün dala yayılmaz.

concept_map.definition: Bir konuğun geldiğinde yararlanması için önceden hazırlanan yiyecek, yol azığı ve ağırlama payıdır. Bu çekirdekten konuğun kendisi, ürün geliri, fazlalık, bağış ve bir araya gelmiş pay anlamları gelişir.

facets.statement: Konuğun yararlanması için yiyecek, yol azığı ve ağırlama payı hazırlanır.
Hazırlanan payla ilişkili olarak konuk kişinin kendisi de adlandırılır.
Hazır pay düşüncesi ürün geliri, fazlalık, bereket ve bağış anlamlarına uzanır.
Bir araya toplanmış pay, konuk için hazırlanmış toplu yiyeceğe benzetilerek anlatılır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Ortak anlatım konuğa hazırlanan yiyecek, azık ve ağırlamayı temel alır; konuk adı, ürün geliri ve fazlalığı, bol verme, topluluğun geçim payları ve birikmiş pay bu hazırlık düşüncesinden gelişir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, insanlara veya bir topluluğa zamanın akışı içinde gelip çatan ağır sıkıntıyı ve bunun çoğulunu açıkça tanımlar. Verilen dal çerçevesi olayın ağırlığını, dışarıdan gelişini ve etkilenen insanları doğru korur.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam başa gelen ağır bir sıkıntıyla sınırlıdır; sıradan fiziksel iniş ya da konuk için hazırlanan pay bu dala girmez.
